fidelity: F1b — Flue Loss (H2O-rich exhaust) + Condensing/Non-Condensing + Standby
source: Hy4Heat WP6 (2021); BEIS UK Hydrogen Heating Trials (2022); Cellek & Pinarbasi (2018) Int. J. Hydrogen Energy 43, 1194-1207; Gas Quality Harmonisation (ACER 2021); Woolley et al. (2022) Appl. Energy.

HHV_H2_MJ_kg.notes: Difference = latent heat of H2O in products

excess_air_ratio.description: Excess air ratio lambda for H2 combustion
excess_air_ratio.notes: H2 burns cleanly; slightly richer than NG for NOx control

T_flue_noncond.notes: Above dew point (~55-58 degC for H2; H2O partial pressure higher than NG)

T_flue_cond.notes: Below dew point; condensate formed; latent heat partially recovered

flue_gas_cp.description: Specific heat of H2O-rich flue gas
flue_gas_cp.notes: Higher than NG flue (~1.05) because H2 combustion products are ~100% H2O

standby_loss_fraction.description: Standby heat loss fraction of Q_rated
